messages:
Maya (sec): heads up — we rolled a targeted RBAC refactor for service principals overnight. main change: the old broad `service_account.admin` was split into smaller roles (redwood.kms.access, redwood.model.deploy, redwood.logs.read). This is live in prod from 03/19 00:00 UTC. :lock:

Jonathan (eng-platform): thanks — any known hitlist? which workloads might see 403s? :eyes:

Maya (sec): primary impact is any integration that relied on `service_account.admin` to list or sign with KMS keys. short list we tracked: embeddings-pipeline, offline-eval-runner, and a handful of partner connectors. audit shows deny for `kms:ListKeys` and `kms:Decrypt` calls from some service accounts.

Ash (integrations): saw this at 01:12 — our partner connector threw 403s when calling kms.list_keys. error snippet: `403 AccessDenied: caller does not have permission to call kms.ListKeys; requestId=req-8f3a` — rolling a hotfix now to catch and surface clearer error.

Pete (oncall): I created a temporary permissive fallback policy for Dedicated-landed instances to keep customer traffic healthy while we triage. policy name: `tmp/redwood/perm-fallback/2026-03-19`. Will remove once owners confirm. :white_check_mark:

Lara (devex): we need a short troubleshooting guide + SDK example for customers and internal devs. Can someone paste the minimal `sdk.check_permissions()` snippet and the recommended policy matrix?

Maya (sec): excerpt from our internal playbook + minimal checks:

```
# pseudo-Python SDK snippet: check KMS perms before operation
from redwood import RBACClient, KMSClient
rbac = RBACClient(service_account_id=SA)
required = ["redwood.kms.access.list", "redwood.kms.access.decrypt"]
ok = rbac.check_permissions(required)
if not ok:
    raise PermissionError("missing required KMS permissions: %s" % rbac.missing())

# then proceed
kms = KMSClient()
kms.sign(key_id)
```

Also quick CLI for local debug: `rw-rbac simulate --sa $SA --actions kms:list,kms:decrypt` returns allowed/denied and policy paths.

Helen (docs): I'll draft a small section in the SDK auth/permissions page and add an FAQ entry: "I get a 403 when listing KMS keys" -> list steps: run `rw-rbac simulate`, check audit logs in `redwood-audit` (filter `event:kms.ListKeys`), verify SA is bound to `redwood.kms.access` or the new granular roles. Will link sample code above.

Ash (integrations): FYI for troubleshooting if you see inconsistent behavior: some older service tokens still get the legacy mapping via the fallback; other tokens got the new roles. You can check mapping with: `rw-identity describe --sa $SA` which prints effective roles.

Jonathan (eng-platform): can we add an automated CI check to catch perms regression? maybe a tiny GH action that runs `rw-rbac simulate` against smoke-test service accounts on PRs touching infra-auth. We should also add a lint rule in infra repo to avoid using `service_account.admin` in new policies.

Maya (sec): agreed. I'm creating a ticket to add the GH action and policy-lint rule. ticket: SEC-1227. Assigning to @jonathan and @lara for implementation and docs.

Pete (oncall): note for postmortem: incident window 01:12–02:40 UTC, root cause: refactor rollout omitted a mapping for a subset of pre-existing tokens. No data exfil; audit logs show denys only. I'll open a postmortem draft and ping infra owners.

sre-bot: deploy bot: RBAC-refactor v2 deployed to prod at 00:02 UTC — rollout 100% — tags: @maya, infra:auth.

Lara (devex): quick Q — should the SDK change name of the call? right now we have `kms_client.list_keys()`. do we want `kms_client.list_accessible_keys()` to reflect RBAC semantics?

Helen (docs): I vote keep existing name but add `raises PermissionError` section and show `rbac.check_permissions()` as recommended pre-check. Less churn for users.

Ash (integrations): workaround we pushed for now: catch 403 and show customer-facing guidance to request the `redwood.kms.access` role. We'll remove once we confirm fixes.

Maya (sec): final ask: owners please run `rw-rbac simulate` for your service accounts and paste results to the ticket SEC-1227. I'll collect and we can remove the fallback when everyone confirms. thanks all :wave:
